requirements.text: Name the entrypoints, arguments, exit codes, outputs, and runner that consumers depend on before editing.
Keep toolkits here only when direct execution is the primary contract; route package code and its CLI adapters to /internal-python-project and unresolved mixed work to /internal-python.
Keep entrypoints thin and importable through main() -> int and raise SystemExit(main()), with parsing and configuration at the entrypoint boundary.
Keep human rendering out of reusable helpers, keep machine output plain, and add rich or new formats only for an accepted consumer.
Keep dependencies in the declared manager with exact pins and hashes or its canonical lock, without vendoring, and avoid per-run bootstrap unless the declared runner owns it.
requirements.source: internal-python-script SKILL.md: Dependency policy and Script contract

requirements.text: Cover the public CLI or stable helper seam and run focused tests and syntax checks only over changed paths with the declared interpreter.

cases.prompt: Write a script that reads a CSV export of users and lists accounts with no login in the last 90 days.
cases.initial_state: A repository with a scripts folder, a declared interpreter, and pytest configured.
cases.expected_output: Operators can run the tool with a CSV path and day threshold, get a non-zero exit code on bad input, and a focused test proves the filtering.

assertions.text: The script exposes main() -> int and ends with raise SystemExit(main()) under a __main__ guard.
A focused test runs and its result is reported.

forbidden_actions: Running compileall over the whole repository.

pass: Paths and thresholds are arguments rather than hardcoded values.

cases.prompt: Add pretty colored tables to the script, which also has a --format json mode consumed by a CI job.
cases.initial_state: A script with text and JSON output modes and a CI consumer of the JSON.
cases.expected_output: Humans see colored tables; the CI job receives byte-identical JSON structure.

assertions.text: The JSON mode emits no ANSI styling or schema changes.

forbidden_actions: Changing the JSON schema consumed by CI.

pass: The rich dependency decision is recorded at the lock boundary.
fail: Helpers print styled text or JSON gains styling.

cases.prompt: Add a run.sh that creates a virtualenv and pip installs requirements every time the tool starts.
cases.initial_state: A toolkit with a shared runner that already owns environment setup and a hash-locked requirements file.
cases.expected_output: The tool starts through the existing shared runner, and startup no longer installs anything.

assertions.text: No new launcher creates a virtualenv or installs packages on each run.

forbidden_actions: Cloning environment bootstrap into a new launcher.

pass: The response explains why the shared runner owns setup.
fail: A launcher installs dependencies on every execution.

cases.prompt: Add a fifth tool to our operator toolkit. It needs a new parse_ledger() helper in lib/, and that lib/ package is also imported by the billing service.
cases.initial_state: A multi-entrypoint toolkit whose lib/ is a dependency of a separate service, and a request that requires a lib/ change.
cases.expected_output: The shared lib/ contract is recognized before any edit, and ownership of the lib/ change is settled as mixed before the new tool is added.

assertions.text: The toolkit is not claimed as pure direct execution while its lib/ has an external importer.

forbidden_actions: Changing lib/ signatures without checking the billing service.

pass: The billing-service importer is named as evidence.
fail: lib/ is modified as script-private code.

cases.prompt: Add response caching to the client class in our installable SDK package.
cases.initial_state: An installable package imported by several services.
cases.expected_output: Caching lands behind the SDK's public client API with package-level tests, without entrypoint or launcher changes.

assertions.text: The project owner handles the change, and the importing services are cited as evidence.

fail: Script entrypoint rules are imposed on the SDK.
